name: Mera Peak Climbing
sub_region: Solukhumbu District, Koshi Province (Khumbu Himal / Mahalangur, Hinku valley; Makalu Barun National Park on the standard approach)

difficulty.notes: Highest NMA trekking peak. Standard route is glaciated walking: rope up for crevasses on the Mera Glacier, crampons and ice axe, moderate snow slopes (operators cite about 25-35 degrees). No headwall and usually no fixed ropes on the normal line (unlike Island Peak). Difficulty is altitude and a 10-14 h summit day from High Camp, not steep ice. Commercial teams usually tag Mera Central; Mera North is a short further traverse.

duration_days.basis: Full trip Kathmandu-Kathmandu via Lukla and the Hinku valley
duration_days.notes: Standard 18-day plan uses the Paiya-Pangom-Kothe-Khare approach and returns over Zatrwa La (also spelled Zatra La). Compressed 16-17 day versions drop rest days; 20-23 day versions add extra acclimatisation at Khare. A short 3-day climb from Khare exists for already-acclimatised climbers. Alternative walk-in from Bung/Mahakulung is listed on the NMA peak table.

max_altitude_point: Mera Peak (NMA / Himalayan Database height; commercial programmes often aim at Mera North 6,476 m or Mera Central 6,461 m)
start_point: Kathmandu (fly to Lukla, or via Manthali/Ramechhap in peak seasons)

itinerary.notes: Briefing, gear check, NMA permit paperwork.
South of the main EBC trail.

itinerary.notes: Climb high, sleep low before Thangnak.

itinerary.notes: Midnight-2 am start; glacier, snow slopes, Central and/or North summit; descend the same day.

itinerary.route: Thuli Kharka - Zatrwa La (about 4,610 m) - Lukla

best_seasons.notes: NMA royalty is lower in autumn (USD 175) than spring (USD 350). Zatrwa La can hold snow outside the main seasons.

permits.name: NMA climbing permit (royalty) - Mera Peak
permits.fee: USD 350 per person spring (Mar-May); USD 175 autumn (Sep-Nov), winter (Dec-Feb) and summer (Jun-Aug)
permits.valid_from: 2025-09-01 (flat per-person rate replaced old group-size tiers)

permits.name: Garbage deposit (refundable, per team)
permits.fee: USD 500 per team (NMA FAQ: all 27 NMA peaks; matches DoT schedule for peaks below 6,500 m)

permits.name: Makalu Barun National Park entry permit
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,500)
permits.applies_to: foreign nationals on the Hinku/Barun side

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Trek-Card
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person (SAARC and Chinese nationals NPR 2,000)
permits.applies_to: foreign nationals entering via Lukla / Khumbu municipality (route-dependent)
permits.status: VERIFIED (rate); whether every Mera itinerary is charged is UNVERIFIED

guide_requirements: NMA peak permits are issued only through a registered Nepali agency; climbing parties require an NMA-registered guide/sirdar (operator summaries of NMA rules). The 2025 Sixth Amendment requires at least one mountain guide per team on peaks below 8,000 m. The Hinku approach is in the NTB Makalu list for the licensed-guide/TIMS trekking rule; whether TIMS is collected from NMA-permit climbers is UNVERIFIED. Lukla/Zatrwa La sits in Khumbu, where the municipality disputes the national guide mandate.

drives: Kathmandu - Manthali about 4-5 h when Lukla flights are diverted
logistics.notes: Teahouses Paiya to Khare (more basic than the EBC trail); tents at High Camp. Some lodges close outside peak months.

highlights: Hinku valley approach, quieter than the Khumbu EBC trail
Summit panorama of five 8,000 m peaks reported by operators (Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Kanchenjunga, Cho Oyu) on a clear morning
Mera La and the Mera Glacier

First ascent of the trekking-peak massif: May 1953, J. O. M. Roberts and Sen Tenzing (Himalayan Database notes they climbed 'false Mera'; Wikipedia assigns Central to 20 May 1953 and North to 1975, Marcel Jolly, G. Baus and L. Honills)
risks: Altitude: nights at High Camp about 5,780 m; summit above 6,400 m
Crevasses and snow bridges on the Mera Glacier
Weather closing High Camp or Zatrwa La

acclimatization.notes: The Hinku walk-in gains height gradually. Standard plans use a Khare rest/skills day and sometimes a second buffer before High Camp. Extra Khare days in 20-23 day programmes.

unverified: Which summit commercial teams actually stand on (Central 6,461 m vs North 6,476 m). NMA and Himalayan Database list 6,470 m; operators often advertise 6,476 m.
Khare overnight altitude: 4,600 m, 4,945 m and 5,045 m all appear in 2026 operator copy.
Sagarmatha National Park entry: some operators list it for Mera, others only Makalu Barun NP. Standard Paiya-Hinku line leaves the SNP core; treat SNP as not confirmed for this itinerary.
Khumbu Trek-Card on every Mera itinerary (charged if entering via Lukla; operator amounts still sometimes NPR 2,000 — _regulations.json is NPR 3,000).
TIMS collection from Mera climbers holding an NMA permit.
Alpine grade F/PD is operator assessment.
Summit-view claim of five 8,000ers is operator-reported, not independently checked here.
